visualReview.notes: Inspected all 11 final portable/source-terrain views. The individual exterior has twin limestone towers with pale pyramidal roofs, open belfries and green hanging bells, an exposed upper-right bell frame, three clock fields on the right tower, a column-supported projecting balcony above one recessed closed wooden portal, blind niches, central gable, pale metal nave roof, repeated sloping buttresses and lower side/rear masonry. Corrected the detached entrance landing and two glazing panels behind irregular mapped masonry. All entrance column feet now meet the landing; side/rear panes meet the actual wall boundary. Bells, clocks and relief fields are selected geometric approximations.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all 11 final shared-material/geographic views. Five existing 256-square graphs provide weathered limestone, raw limestone, standing-seam metal, lime plaster and wood. Roofs and green bells share metal with linear tints; pyramids and clock fields share plaster. UVs are metric, glass is flat blue-gray and skyline materials use mean tints. Each graph reads once. Unloading leaves zero live model geometries and restores ground. The geographic top view checks the signed mapped plan on flat terrain; portable views show the retained coarse DEM. Ground colors are diagnostic.

Italian-palazzo neighbors are synthetic context, not local mapped buildings.

Actual viewer coverage checks across all six outputs retain the cathedral while leaving north/clock-side neighboring buildings and the open front square uncovered. Exact thresholds, plaza contact and walking fit remain approximate; no road replacement.
